$schemaNote: Format defined in CONFORMANCE-VECTORS.md. Merge vectors: each `given` is an ordered list of synthetic observations (source, kind, run generation, judging/closure flags as DERIVATIONS.md would resolve them) and connection events, fed to the merge function in `ingestSeq` order; `expect` (or `expectSequence` + `then`) is the presented state a correct implementation must produce. Standing vectors: `given.entries` are resolved Attempt facts; `expect` is the assembled Standing (CONTRACTS.md SS5). Data only, no runtime logic (ADR-002/ADR-003, TEST-ARCHITECTURE.md SS3.1).

vectors.description: A field with no new observation in a later message is untouched, not regressed to not-yet.

expect.note: status is unaffected by the unrelated placement observation at ingestSeq 2.

vectors.description: A field never observed stays not-yet; it is never defaulted to unavailable because other fields have values.
A result push supersedes the on-course inference of the same run generation, whatever the ingest order within the run.
An on-course inference arriving after a result row for the same run does not displace it.

expect.note: the late on-course message still carried a blank gate; the result row already had it judged.

vectors.description: While TCP stays connected, a later-ingested XML row does not displace the tcp observation of the same field.

expect.note: the snapshot was written before the penalty was added; a connected TCP is never behind it. The disagreement is surfaced (INV-2b), never adopted.

vectors.description: After TCP disconnects, a snapshot rewrite detected afterwards takes over.

expect.note: a correction (+50 at a gate) made during the outage reaches us only through the snapshot.

vectors.description: After reconnection, a tcp observation from before the outage does not outrank a snapshot read during the outage (the R52 defect of the previous rule).

expect.note: the pre-outage tcp value (ingestSeq 1) lost its continuity; until TCP pushes this race again, the later xml value stays presented.

vectors.description: A tcp observation ingested after reconnection outranks the snapshot again.
With nothing observed on TCP, the snapshot supplies the value, authoritative and final once judging is complete.
A field only the snapshot carries is presented from it, whatever TCP does; a field only TCP carries, from TCP. Two fields, so an adapter that skips one cannot pass vacuously (R4a).
A row whose Rank is empty has no placement, whatever its RankOrder: a marked row's moving sort key is never presented and never pushed (ADR-017 D2, S4-2).

expect.note: rawRankOrder is informational: the resolved placement is null in both rows, so the second snapshot changes nothing.

vectors.description: A result pushed before the last gate is judged is provisional, and settles when the judged push arrives: ranking with incomplete penalties on.
With ranking on incomplete penalties off, the first push follows the last gate and is final at once.
Without a configured course, judging completeness cannot be read: the value stays provisional until the run is closed.

A second run's placement, pairTotal and countingRun carried over from run 1 become provisional at the Attempt's first listing in run 2, staged or started, without a regression (ADR-017 D4, S1-12; CONTRACTS §1.2, §3.2 round 20). Bib 9 is staged (`at-start`) and then started; bib 10 is started with no staging, `false -> true` at that listing.
status is never provisional: neither the on-course inference nor a finished status with judging still incomplete (ADR-017 D4, S1-11).
Before the result push, the inferred total keeps updating as trailing gate judgements arrive.
A settled disagreement between retained sources is surfaced as a diagnostic and never changes the presented value.

During a TCP outage a snapshot takes over (rule 2) only if its content is newer than TCP's last observation of the field: a rewrite detected within one poll interval of the push may predate it and is refused; the next rewrite supersedes.

context.note: closes DERIVATIONS §10 item 8; TCP's last push corrected the gate penalty from 2 to 0 just before the outage, the first snapshot still carries 2.

expect.note: first snapshot: content age 10:41:02 - 5 s = 10:40:57 < 10:40:59.5, refused, tcp stays; second snapshot: 10:41:32 > 10:40:59.5, presented (a 50 given during the outage).

vectors.description: A snapshot whose content age is unknown (changedAfter null: a first read) never displaces or retracts a tcp observation, even after a tcp outage; it presents what no tcp observation presents. The next rewrite, whose changedAfter follows the outage, settles the rest: a repeated refused value is presented, and the Attempt whose row is absent from that table is removed (INV-7, an absent XML row; maintainer, 2026-11-11 and 2026-11-12).

context.note: Attempts A = :9, B = :10, C = :11. A and C have tcp results; B has none.

expect.note: first snapshot: changedAfter null fails the guard, so A (84 vs 86) and C (a retraction by a present, empty row) stay tcp; B has no tcp observation and is presented from xml. second: changedAfter 10:41:32 follows the outage and the tcp pushes, A's repeated value is presented; C's row is absent from a table that carries other rows, every tcp observation of C predates the content age and C is off course, so C's Attempt is removed.

vectors.description: Two athletes credited with each other's finishes are corrected in the results grid: the later push of the same source supersedes for both, including the one whose true finish is the earlier (ARCHITECTURE Scenario I). The previous edition's event-time floor would have refused that row on the XML side.

context.note: recorded shape: jarni-ne-odp 12:55-13:05 (three shifted back one by one; not yet replayed). The nkz-19so 42/43 event was a penalty move, not a finish swap.

expect.note: bib 42's corrected row carries 84.0 where 90.0 was presented; same source, later ingest, presented. TCP rows carry no finish time (D1); the finish moving earlier shows on the XML/on-course side and is never compared for precedence.

vectors.description: A real, asserted zero is structurally distinct from not-yet and unavailable: the direct fix for Exhibit 5.
unavailable{reason} is an explicit determination and persists as a state distinct from not-yet.

expect.note: no course layout is configured for this Phase (CONTRACTS.md SS2.12).

vectors.description: A person with no registry identity carries externalId null inside a known members value, never an unavailable envelope, and the entry stays fully renderable.

expect.note: members is the wrapped unit (CONTRACTS.md SS1.2, SS2.5); a null inside its value is the trichotomy's not-applicable stated as the type says, not as an envelope.

vectors.description: A correction to who raced under a bib is a normal known-to-known transition, not a structural rebind.

expect.note: attemptId is unchanged: it is keyed on (phaseId, bib).

vectors.description: Re-delivering an identical observation does not alter presented state or notify.

expect.note: the rotation re-sends the same row 30 s later; one client-visible change only.

vectors.description: A wall-clock jump backward does not let the earlier-clocked, later-arrived observation lose: ordering is by ingestSeq.
An optimistic write is presented the instant it is submitted.
The echo matching the requested value confirms the write.
An echo that disagrees becomes presented, and the write records the mismatch.
A pending write whose run generation is replaced by a re-run resolves to superseded.
A no-echo correction (provisional:false) is not displaced by a re-delivery of the value the source already held.
A no-echo correction is displaced by a result observation that changes its source's retained value: a genuine later upstream correction.
A new start for a bib whose run is recorded starts generation 2 and retracts the run-scoped fields explicitly.
After a re-run starts, a result row describing the replaced run (finish before the new start) is retained as history, never presented.

After a re-run starts, a TCP row (no finish time) carrying a time is the replaced run's unless the new generation's on-course finish arrives with the same time; a row arriving before that finish is retained and attributed when the finish arrives, as recorded (result push 108 ms before the on-course finish, nkz-19so C1M_BR1_19 bib 7). ADR-017 D1.

expect.note: the 88.2 row arrived before the generation's on-course finish: retained, not yet attributed

the 85.0 row is the replaced run: retained, never presented; the 88.2 row, retained for 108 ms, is attributed when the on-course finish arrives with the same time and is presented with that finish as eventTime.

vectors.description: finished -> on-course is legal only together with a run increment; without one it is refused.

expect.note: an on-course observation without evidence of a new start (no new dtStart, no cleared row) is not a re-run.

vectors.description: A slalom athlete leaving the on-course list with no finish becomes left-without-finish; the reason is not inferred.
A no-result mark set on a silent path arrives in the snapshot and supersedes the TCP left-without-finish, while TCP stays connected.
The exception is narrow: an XML mark never supersedes a TCP status that is itself a finish or a mark.
While the Attempt is on the on-course list, a blank result-row cell never overwrites a cell the on-course stream has judged.

expect.note: the last gate was judged clean on the on-course stream; upstream sends no result push for that until the run closes (~20 s).

vectors.description: After the Attempt has left the on-course list, the result row's gate vector is authoritative whole: a later correction lands.
A row previously present with a mark vanishes from a complete TCP push of its race: the mark is retracted, the athlete is not-started.
The recorded sequence: DNS pushed, row vanishes, athlete starts, finishes and is placed.
A non-snapshot observation (a single-row fragment, or an on-course message) never retracts: absence in it is omission.

context.note: UDP fragments are not consumed at all (ADR-011); the vector pins the rule for any implementation that ever parses one.

vectors.description: A complete push of another race is omission for this race.
A push in start-list mode (no row placed or marked) states that nobody has a result: every results-sourced result in the race is retracted. This is what "delete all results" produces.
A push of the race that lacks the row does not retract an on-course inference: the row may not be written yet.

In a paired second run, a row present with an empty time and no mark retracts run 2 — outcome, gates and any mark in status — while the combined placement follows the row (recorded: a second-run DNS cleared in place, then the athlete raced).

An XML row emptied for an Attempt known from a results-table observation retracts, even while TCP is connected, provided the rewrite was detected more than one poll interval after the tcp observation.

context.note: the recorded jury-invalidated run (C1M_BR1_19 bib 7, later re-run): cleared in the XML five minutes before TCP's rotation showed it.

vectors.description: In a first-run race a TCP row present with no time and no mark states no result: the recorded jury invalidation wiped the row in place eight minutes after closure (nkz-19so C1M_BR1_19 bib 7, 10:56:58Z). The vector never lists the Attempt on course, so status falls to not-started.

expect.note: the row is present but carries nothing: a retraction, not an omission (INV-1 would have kept the score). Two messages: the creation carrying the result, then the retraction. Run 2 of the same athlete, two hours later, is the generation case.

vectors.description: An XML rewrite detected within one poll interval of the tcp observation may predate the push: it does not retract. A later rewrite does.

An XML snapshot that lists other rows of the race and not this Attempt's removes the Attempt, when its content age is later than every tcp observation of it and it is off course (ADR-015 Revisions 5 and 6): one attempt.deleted, no attempt.updated for it.
An absent XML row is under the content-age guard: a rewrite that may predate the push neither removes nor retracts; a later rewrite removes the Attempt (ADR-015 Revisions 5 and 6).

An XML table with no rows at all retracts nothing, whatever its content age: one read of the lagging source does not clear a race (ADR-015 Revision 5). The core raises xml-table-emptied in the admin log, which no vector reads.
A row that returns to the XML table after its Attempt was removed creates a new Attempt, presented from xml by the ordinary rules, run 1 (ADR-015 Revision 6).

An Attempt known only from a start-list row is removed when a later XML snapshot of its race lists other rows and not its own: a competitor deleted, moved or re-bibbed before starting (ADR-015 Revision 6). A retraction would have changed nothing; the removal is one attempt.deleted.

An Attempt in the on-course set is never removed by an XML snapshot that lacks its row, whatever the content age: TCP still lists it (ADR-015 Revision 6). It holds no result, so nothing is retracted either.
A finish taken away on the on-course grid: the on-course stream lists the bib running again, later pushes still carry the stale time, the real finish lifts it.

context.note: recorded: a false leader for 31.5 s on the wire; the contract shows none. TCP rows carry no finish time: the contradicted finish is matched by run time (ADR-017 D1).

vectors.description: After the on-course stream lifts a contradiction by showing a finish, rows still carrying the contradicted finish stay unpresented; only rows carrying the new finish present (ADR-017 D1, S1-20).

expect.note: the stale 48.64 row re-pushed after the lift is still the contradicted finish by run time: retained, unpresented; the inference stands until a row carries 88.96.

vectors.description: A contradicted finish takes countingRun to not-yet (INV-2d); countingRun is XML-only (INV-2 rule 3), so no tcp observation of it exists for rule 2 to prefer: it stays not-yet through the lift by the real TCP row, and the next XML row that does not carry the contradicted finish presents it again, source xml. Recorded nkz-19so K1M_BR2_19:67 (#314, opponent finding 13): XML BetterRunNr 1 restated at 09:37:12.135Z (first stated 07:50:23.567Z), false TCP finish 9.16 at 09:37:48.972Z, stream finish at 09:37:49.229Z, contradiction at 09:38:00.824Z, snapshot of 09:38:22.255Z carrying the false finish and BetterRunNr 2 (unpresented whole), re-pushed false row at 09:39:05.373Z, real finish 91.83 at 09:39:11.621Z, snapshot of 09:39:32.365Z with the real finish and BetterRunNr 1. The run-2 penalty the later snapshot carries is elided so the vector pins countingRun alone.
A row carrying a mark and a time presents no-result: a duplicate finish was resolved upstream by a DNF while both rows kept the time.
An XML snapshot written mid-correction shows one finish on two bibs: both are presented as upstream's state, a duplicate-finish diagnostic is raised, and the next TCP push resolves it.

context.note: recorded: bogus leaders were published for about 2 min; the contract shows upstream's state with the hazard visible. The resolving TCP rows carry no finish time (D1): once they supersede the snapshot's rows under rule 2, no two presented finishes share an eventTime, and the diagnostic clears.

vectors.description: The operator re-baseline discards retained tcp knowledge for the race, presents the current XML snapshot, and lets the next TCP push refill.

context.note: the DNS on bib 53 was deleted on a silent path; TCP still carried it. After the re-baseline the tcp slot is empty, so rule 2 presents xml until the next push.

vectors.description: A re-baseline keeps run generations, verification state and pending writes; only upstream knowledge is rebuilt.
On the live tier an explicit not-yet in a partial push resets the field; omission leaves it untouched.
The on-course set is ordered by courseOrder, shrinks when an Attempt leaves the list, and each change is pushed as one oncourse.updated.

context.note: Cross: leaving the list changes no status, so the set is the only signal a client has.

vectors.description: The on-course set is upstream's list: a finish changes status, not membership; the Attempt leaves the set only when upstream stops listing it, about 20 s later, and that oncourse.updated is the closure the write rule's retry waits for.

expect.note: one push when the Attempt entered the set, one when upstream stopped listing it; the finish produced an attempt.updated, never an oncourse.updated.

vectors.description: An Attempt staged and then removed before any start returns to not-started, never left-without-finish (ADR-017, S1-16; recorded: a bib staged 5 s into the next day's race).
A second-run athlete holds a combined placement from run 1; its running ticks never re-send the standing, whose entry result is pending while on course (ADR-017 D3, S1-25).

expect.note: K1M_BR2_19 has a phase and a pair standing (§5): two serialised changes — the first snapshot, and the run-2 start that made the carried-over fields provisional — give four standing.updated; the three running ticks produce attempt.updated only, and both entries' result is pending throughout.

vectors.description: On the live tier a bare Entry body is wrapped by the store: known values carry source bridge; a null Entry field becomes not-applicable; a member's null externalId stays null inside members.
A DELETE on the live tier removes the Attempt and its standing entries, idempotently, and emits attempt.deleted.

A mark carried from before a re-run is withheld on any row of the new generation, attributed or not: here the stale DNF row arrives before run 2's on-course finish (the usual order), then the finish attributes it, then a later, different mark (dsq) is presented. ADR-017 D1, R16.

context.note: upstream does not clear an old DNF when a re-run finishes over it (source; no recorded instance). The spike's core presented the stale DNF in this order because it checked stale marks only after attribution (opponent review R16).

expect.note: the row arrived before the finish: its mark equals the remembered one and is withheld; the athlete is still running
a different mark is presented and the stale-mark diagnostic clears (DERIVATIONS §4.12).

vectors.description: On the live tier the on-course set is replaced whole by each push, in the pushed order; an unknown attemptId is stubbed; each push emits one oncourse.updated; identical re-push is a no-op.

context.note: bib 58 was stubbed by the first push and stays as an Attempt after leaving the set.

vectors.description: On the live tier the latest bridge observation of outcome is presented: running values in order, then the finished duration; nothing is cleared when pushes stop.

context.note: the bridge pushes presented values in its own ingest order and coalesces to one per Attempt per second; the store presents the latest (INV-6).

vectors.description: A write confirmed by echo and later changed upstream: the field shows the new value and the WriteRequest stays confirmed; confirmed is about the echo, not permanence.
A classification push replaces the Phase's rows whole; the classification Standing is assembled from them as delivered and dated by the push's asOf.

context.note: entry C dropped out on recalculation; no Attempt exists for a classification Phase.

vectors.description: A placed result row with no finish time in a duration-scored Phase is an operator-typed row: outcome is not-applicable, placement is presented, the time is never shown.

context.note: recorded junior time-trial rows: Time 100.00 for everyone, real ranks and Q; rank x 1000 typed in later.

vectors.description: underReview and provisional are independent fields.
In a second-run race a DNS mark describes run 2 only: status dns, placement still the combined one.
Run 1's Attempt is untouched by anything in run 2's messages.
A cold server with no live observation recovers run 1 from the snapshot, authoritative.
Run 1 never observed and the snapshot unreadable: unavailable only once run 2 has been observed, not-yet before.
Before the operator enters the heat order, the outcome is not-yet and the status stays on-course, even after the heat left the on-course list.
The Cross ordinal is upstream's placement within the heat, never the finish order encoded in Time: a faulted athlete who finished first is placed after clean finishers.

expect.note: finish position 1 (Time "1.00") but two faults; upstream places the athlete third.

vectors.description: A later correction to heat order lands even after the next heat started; a stale snapshot row cannot undo it while TCP is connected.
official -> revised is legal directly.
A post-finish disqualification is legal, not a rejected regression.
Entries sort by relayed order and show relayed rank; a single-run tie keeps its shared rank with upstream's sequence.
A combined tie broken upstream by the non-counting run is relayed as is and is not an anomaly.
An entry without placement is listed after all placed ones with null rank and order; no server-computed rank.

expect.note: A finished faster than B but has no placement yet (first push not ingested); it is not ranked by us. Unplaced entries order by status then bib: finished before dns.

vectors.description: Age-category standing: filter the class standing; a placed entry's rank and order are its position among the category's placed entries in class order, Canoe123's numbering, so entries tied on class rank get consecutive category ranks (maintainer, 2026-11-12).

An age-category standing lists the category's unplaced entries after its placed ones, with null rank and order, in step 3's order, as on a printed result list (maintainer, 2026-11-12). Entries of another category are not listed.

expect.note: Recorded shape: jarni-ne-odp C1M_BR1_19, bib 64 DNF in category ZM after the placed entries; its upstream CatRnk 9 is a list position, not a rank. Unplaced entries order by status in AttemptStatus declaration order (dns before dnf), then bib.

vectors.description: When the snapshot's own category rank arrives and differs from the assembled one, an anomaly is recorded and the assembled rank stays.
Relayed order placing a strictly worse result ahead of a strictly better one is recorded; the relayed order still stands.
Cross scopes are never checked mechanically: fault-based order is upstream's rule.
behindSeconds is the ranked value minus the leader's; provisional and underReview are copied from the Attempt.
A check reads verified while the presented penalty equals the value seen at check time, and stale once a later correction changes it.

null and 0 are distinct: a check made while the gate was unjudged is stale once it is judged clean; a check made against 0 is stale once the gate is retracted to null; when gates is not known the presented value is null.

context.note: gates 6 and 8 model the state after a retraction (ADR-015): the check is never deleted, its status follows the presented value.

vectors.description: A team gate penalty is the member sum; the check compares the sum.
A new run generation starts with no checks; the earlier generation's check stays readable under its own run.
A result moved from bib 55 to bib 56: bib 55's check becomes stale against its retracted gates; bib 56 has no check.

A start moved while the athlete is still on course, with no finish and no row, is a correction inside the generation, not a re-run: the start deleted and given again (recorded: nkz-20ne K1M_BR1_20:115, 5 s apart) and the start moved 38 s earlier mid-run (recorded: jarni-so-do K1M_BR1_18:138, Time 0 to 89). DERIVATIONS 4.11; ADR-013 Revision 4.

The recorded order (jarni-so-odp C1M_BR2_18:56): the corrected row (120.98, rank 60) is pushed 101 ms before the listing that carries the moved start, the same dtFinish and Time 120.98. The row supersedes (same source, later ingested), the listing changes nothing, run stays 1, placement is never not-yet. DERIVATIONS 4.11 "Both arrival orders".

The other order: the correcting listing before the 120.98 row. The listing is a correction (run 1, no contradicted-finish since dtFinish is present, the first row still presented by rule 1); the row supersedes when it arrives. Same end state as row-first. DERIVATIONS 4.11.

The one recorded re-run (nkz-19so C1M_BR1_19:7) by its listings: run 1 raced (row 55 ms before the finish listing, as recorded) and closed, the row retracted by a start-list push, staged with no start, then a listing with a different start and no finish while the generation is recorded: run increments. A retraction does not un-record. DERIVATIONS 4.11, 4.12; ADR-013 Revision 4.

A re-delivery is an observation in its own right: after an outage in which an xml value displaced the tcp one, the connect burst (or a rotation) re-sending the same tcp value regains precedence and is pushed as the envelope change it is. INV-5 as restated in round 19: the no-op is about a value already presented from that source.

Seven recorded Attempts reached their first start with a DNS or CAP on the table, six of them cleared before the start (written here as a first run). The first start is no change, and a later start moved earlier with no finish is a correction: run stays 1, no re-run. DERIVATIONS 4.11 "The recorded start"; ADR-013 Revision 4.

expect.note: a listing with dtStart empty displaces no mark presented from the table

vectors.description: A mark rule 2's content-age guard refuses shows nowhere: `no-result` is the presentation of the presented `status`, never a field of the row (CONTRACTS §2.6, round 20). The xml row's mark is retained with its whole row; the next rewrite whose content age postdates the tcp observation presents `status` and `outcome` together, in one `attempt.updated`.

The guard compares content age, and a `tcp` row's content age is the observedAt of its latest delivery (INV-2c, INV-5; round 20): a rotation re-sending the identical row advances it, so an xml retraction whose content (150) predates the re-delivery (200) is ignored for every field the row carried, none of them retracted and the others kept. A later rewrite (250) retracts all three.

`not-started` is presented from the first results-table row that names the Attempt, a start-list row included, with that row's envelope (CONTRACTS §3.2, DERIVATIONS §4): `status` is `not-yet` only for an Attempt no row and no listing has named. A start list names the Attempt; it is not on course.

A classification table emptied upstream is no retraction: a snapshot with no rows, from either source, changes nothing, so the Standing stays as last built and nothing is pushed (DERIVATIONS §4.10; maintainer, 2026-11-06). Rows arriving again replace it whole.

context.note: no Attempt exists for a classification Phase; asOf is not read directly, a Standing being pushed exactly when its serialised form changes (CONTRACTS §5).
